steps.u: We need rate limiting on the public API: 100 requests per minute per API key, with proper 429 responses and a Retry-After header.

steps.a: A fixed window counter allows bursts at window edges. A sliding window log is exact but costly. I will use a token bucket per key in Redis with an atomic Lua script, which gives smooth limits and one round trip.

i.content:
const script = `local t=redis.call('time') ... return {allowed, retry}`
export const rateLimit = (limit=100, per=60) => async (req,res,next)=>{ const [ok,retry]=await redis.eval(script,1,'rl:'+req.apiKey,limit,per); if(!ok){ res.set('Retry-After',String(retry)); return res.status(429).json({error:'rate_limited'}) } next() }

it('returns 429 with Retry-After after 100 calls', async()=>{})
it('isolates keys', async()=>{})

reference.summary: Added per-API-key rate limiting of 100 requests per minute to the public API, using a Redis token bucket in an atomic Lua script, returning 429 with a Retry-After header.

decisions.choice: token bucket in an atomic Lua script over a fixed window counter
decisions.reason: fixed windows allow bursts at the edges while the script gives smooth limits in one round trip
